clue.text: Bigwig abandons a follower in haste

indicators.note: to abandon something is to leave it behind, so a letter drops out of the word

parts.note: a bigwig is a famous, important person
the letter that follows A in the alphabet

explanation.surface: An important person hurries off, leaving an aide behind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A follower' is not a disciple but the letter after A; take it out of CELEBRITY to leave CELERITY.
explanation.definitionFit: Celerity is a formal word for swiftness or speed of movement.

clue.text: Vehicle bearing

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a horse-drawn coach or railway coach
second meaning: deportment, the way one holds oneself

explanation.definitionFit: A carriage is a wheeled conveyance, and a person's carriage is their posture or deportment.

clue.text: Eros ridiculed this security man, proverbially

definitions.text: Eros ridiculed this security man, proverbially

parts.note: surface reading: the Greek god mocked a guard
setter's reading: Eros is Love, and the proverb says Love laughs at the man who fits locks

explanation.surface: The god of love mocked a security guard.
explanation.walkthrough: The proverb is 'Love laughs at locksmiths': no lock keeps lovers apart. Eros stands for Love and ridiculed for laughs at.
explanation.definitionFit: The tradesman who makes and fixes locks is the security worker named in the old saying.

clue.text: Transgress again, by gum!

parts.note: the prefix meaning again
commit a wrong

explanation.surface: A shocked exclamation at someone sinning a second time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'By gum!' is a mild northern English oath, hiding the definition gum.
explanation.definitionFit: Resin is the sticky substance exuded by trees, a kind of gum.

clue.text: Having will to remove capital holdings

indicators.note: a word's capital is its head, its opening letter

parts.note: the opening letter of the word
property, possessions

explanation.surface: A wealthy person makes a will to strip the family of its assets.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads backwards: the answer, to remove its capital letter, leaves holdings. Taking off the initial T from the answer leaves ESTATE.
explanation.definitionFit: Testate is the legal term for someone who died having made a valid will.

clue.text: Seafood starters of sole, crab and mussel, price inclusive

indicators.note: the starters of words are their opening letters, as starters open a meal

parts.words: sole, crab and mussel, price inclusive
parts.note: the opening letter of each of these six words

explanation.surface: A seafood restaurant menu offering starters of sole, crab and mussels, with the price all-in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Starters' sits naturally on a menu, but here it means first letters, and even 'and' and 'inclusive' contribute.
explanation.definitionFit: Scampi are breaded or fried langoustine tails, a common British seafood dish.

clue.text: Kind of music produced by leading group with mid-scale accompaniment

parts.note: class one, the top category

indicators.note: mid means middle, so only the central letters are kept

parts.note: the inner letters, once the outer ones are dropped

explanation.surface: Music performed by a top band with a melody running up and down the scale.
explanation.walkthrough: Class I, Roman one, is the leading group or first class.
explanation.definitionFit: Classical music is the serious Western tradition of composers like Mozart and Beethoven.

clue.text: Unexpected gift from German Navy

indicators.note: from means taken out of, so the letters come from inside the phrase

parts.note: the letters run across the two words

explanation.surface: A windfall comes from the German fleet.
explanation.definitionFit: Manna, the food God sent the Israelites in the desert, means any unexpected benefit or windfall.

clue.text: Impact of bitter when propping-up batting order

indicators.note: in a down clue, propping up means sitting underneath, so this piece comes second

parts.note: a cricket side batting is in
the mark left by something biting, a dent

explanation.surface: The effect of a pint of bitter beer on a cricket team's batting order.
explanation.walkthrough: Bitter is a British pale ale. The setter seems to mean 'biter': a dent is the impact, the tooth-mark, of something that bites.
explanation.definitionFit: An indent is an official requisition or order for goods or supplies.

clue.text: Large nurse in Belgium

definitions.note: a phrase standing for a place found in Belgium

parts.note: outsize, the clothing size abbreviation
look after

explanation.surface: A big nurse working in Belgium.
explanation.definitionFit: Ostend is a North Sea port and resort on the Belgian coast.

clue.text: Tries to get to sleep but on these it's icy!

definitions.meaning: first meaning: sways a baby gently back and forth to send it off
second meaning: a drink served 'on the' ice cubes

explanation.surface: Someone struggling to drift off finds the conditions frosty.
explanation.walkthrough: A whisky 'on the rocks' is served over ice; that idiom supplies the second, cryptic meaning.
explanation.definitionFit: A parent soothes an infant towards slumber with swaying motion, and ice cubes in a glass are called by the same word.

clue.text: Suffered without let-up

definitions.meaning: first meaning: underwent, as of an injury or loss

explanation.surface: Someone endured pain that never eased.
explanation.definitionFit: One sustains an injury, meaning undergoes it, and sustained effort is unbroken, continuous effort over time.

clue.text: Numb as with intense movement

indicators.note: movement shifts things about, so the letters are moved into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A limb goes numb after strenuous exercise.
explanation.definitionFit: Insensate means lacking physical sensation, unable to feel anything.

clue.text: Lover depicted by Bard embracing Imogen initially

indicators.note: to embrace is to hold in one's arms, so one piece wraps around another

parts.note: Shakespeare is called the Swan of Avon

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letter of the word it follows

parts.note: the opening letter of the name

explanation.surface: A romantic suitor portrayed by Shakespeare holding Imogen, heroine of his Cymbeline.
explanation.walkthrough: Ben Jonson called Shakespeare the 'Sweet Swan of Avon', which lets Bard stand for SWAN.
explanation.definitionFit: A swain is a poetic word for a young male suitor or sweetheart, often a country youth.

clue.text: Catch sight of proceeds irregularly accepted in notes

indicators.note: something accepted in is taken inside, so one piece sits within another

parts.note: G and E are both musical notes
walks unevenly, with a halting gait

explanation.surface: Spotting irregular takings slipped in among the banknotes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Proceeds' looks like money, going with 'notes', but it is a verb for going forward.
explanation.definitionFit: To glimpse is to see something briefly or partially, just catching sight of it.

clue.text: Relish acceptance of tip coming up in flutter

indicators.note: acceptance means taking in, so one piece goes inside

parts.note: a taste or liking for something

indicators.note: in a down clue, coming up means read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone enjoys a betting tip, placing a small wager on it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flutter' is a British word for a small bet, fitting tip; here it is the heart's flutter.
explanation.definitionFit: To palpitate is for the heart to beat rapidly or flutter.

clue.text: Clarify river to accommodate fish

indicators.note: to accommodate a guest is to house it, so one piece goes inside another

parts.note: the Dee is a river in Wales, England and Scotland
a common food fish

explanation.surface: An instruction to make room in a river for fish, after clarifying the water.
explanation.definitionFit: To decode is to turn a coded or obscure message into plain meaning, making it clear.

clue.text: Lowering by digger and demolition

indicators.note: demolition knocks things to pieces, so the letters are broken up and rebuilt

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A site is brought down by a mechanical excavator and demolition crew.
explanation.definitionFit: Degrading means debasing or bringing down in rank or esteem, a figurative lowering.

clue.text: Perception shown by rowers securing approval

indicators.note: to secure is to hold fast, so one piece holds the other inside

parts.note: a racing boat crewed by eight rowers
a word of assent

explanation.surface: A rowing crew wins the nod of approval for its keen awareness.
explanation.definitionFit: Eyesight is the faculty of seeing, visual perception.

clue.text: As long as there is money in cards?

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the other

parts.note: a card game for four players
L is the abbreviation for pounds sterling, from Latin libra

explanation.surface: A card player keeps going only while there is cash on the table.
explanation.walkthrough: The L sits in the middle: WHI-L-ST.
explanation.definitionFit: Whilst is a British form of while, a conjunction meaning during the time that.

clue.text: Move start of play in court upset

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the other
in a down clue, upset means turned upside down, so read from the bottom

parts.note: the standard abbreviation for court
Act I, the opening part of a stage play

explanation.surface: A sporting move from the start of a match on a tennis court goes wrong.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Play' suggests sport with 'court', but it is a stage play, which starts with Act I. Only the court abbreviation is reversed: TC holds ACTI.
explanation.definitionFit: A tactic is a manoeuvre or ploy, a calculated move to gain advantage.

clue.text: Casualty needs to come down by rope

parts.note: drop to the ground
a guy is a rope used to steady a tent or mast

explanation.surface: An injured climber has to be lowered on a rope.
explanation.definitionFit: A fall guy is someone who ends up taking the blame or the loss, a victim of circumstances.

clue.text: Surrender offer — it's disastrous

indicators.note: a disastrous outcome leaves things wrecked, so the letters are thrown into disorder

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: An offer to give up turns out a calamity.
explanation.definitionFit: To forfeit is to give up or lose a right or possession, typically as a penalty.

clue.text: Two little nursery characters brought up by bird

indicators.note: in a down clue, brought up means raised from the bottom, so the letters run upwards

parts.note: first small fairy-tale being
second small fairy-tale being, a fairy

explanation.surface: A pair of small children's-story figures raised by a bird.
explanation.walkthrough: The yaffle is the green woodpecker, named for its laughing call; it was also a wooden woodpecker in the British children's TV show Bagpuss.
explanation.definitionFit: Yaffle is a dialect name for the green woodpecker, a British bird.

clue.text: Calculators providing heads to columns

definitions.meaning: second meaning: in architecture, flat slabs crowning a column's capital

explanation.surface: Adding machines that print headings over columns of figures.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests spreadsheet columns, but the second sense is architectural: the abacus is the slab on top of a capital.
explanation.definitionFit: The plural of abacus covers both the counting frames and the slabs topping classical pillars.

clue.text: She's sainted — times without number

definitions.note: a description of a female saint, standing for her name

indicators.note: without in its old sense means outside, so one piece wraps around the other

parts.note: eras, periods
N stands for an unspecified number in maths

explanation.surface: A woman is declared a saint countless times over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Without number' reads as countless, but here without means outside: AGES goes around N.
explanation.definitionFit: Agnes is the name of a virgin martyr venerated as a saint, Saint Agnes of Rome.

clue.text: Sings about America in merry parties

indicators.note: about means around, so the first piece goes around the second

parts.note: carols, as in singing Christmas songs
the United States of America

explanation.surface: Someone sings patriotic songs about America at lively celebrations.
explanation.definitionFit: Carousals are drunken, boisterous revels, rowdy drinking parties.

clue.text: Rumba dancing in shadow

indicators.note: dancing moves about, so the letters are moved into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Couples perform a Latin dance in the dim light.
explanation.definitionFit: The umbra is the darkest central part of a shadow, especially in an eclipse.

clue.text: Romance of fast sea in turmoil

definitions.note: a verb here: to invent romantic stories

indicators.note: turmoil is wild disorder, so the letters are thrown into confusion

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written; it doubles as part of the indicator phrase in the surface

explanation.surface: A tale of love on a racing, stormy sea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Romance' looks like a noun, but it is the verb meaning to tell fanciful stories.
explanation.definitionFit: To romance in its verb sense is to embellish or daydream, imagining things that are not true.

clue.text: Transport vessel without name

indicators.note: without in its old sense means outside, so one piece wraps around the other

parts.note: a two-masted sailing ship
N is the abbreviation for name

explanation.surface: A ship used for carrying goods has no name painted on it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Without' reads as lacking, but here it means outside: BRIG goes around N.
explanation.definitionFit: To bring is to carry or convey something to a place, a verb sense of transport.

clue.text: Followed girl into Close

indicators.note: into places the first piece inside the second

parts.note: close as a noun, the finish
a girl's name

explanation.surface: Someone trailed a young woman into a cul-de-sac.
explanation.walkthrough: The capital C makes Close look like a street name; it is the noun meaning finish.
explanation.definitionFit: Ensued means came afterwards or resulted, happening next in sequence.

clue.text: Returning craft in view, going in the same direction

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the other

parts.note: something seen, a vista

indicators.note: returning means going back, so the word is read from the end

parts.note: skill, artistry

explanation.surface: A boat heading home comes into sight on a steady course.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Craft' suggests a boat, but here it is skill.
explanation.definitionFit: A straight course or line keeps the same direction without bending or turning.
